data.narrative:
Stacked Energy, founded by Dylan Erb and Sumitha Durairaj, is a Series A climate and energy company that has raised $98M to date. The valuation universe for frontier energy consists of 1 public comparable (Linamar, ticker LNZA) and 8 private peers including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix.

The analysis applies one triangulation method. Stage-progression valuation uses the $98M total raised as a baseline proxy and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for progression from Series A to subsequent stages, yielding an implied valuation of $196M. A peer-median approach was not applicable; while 8 same-sector companies exist, none met the narrow filtering criteria (same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier parity) required to establish a reliable 3+ comparable set. Relying on all-sector medians would introduce excessive methodological noise.

The triangulated valuation range is $167M (low) to $225M (high), with a median of $196M. This range reflects the stage-progression methodology and reasonable sensitivity bounds. Key uncertainties include the absence of tight-fit peer metrics, the private status of most comparables limiting observable transaction data, and the nascent stage at which valuation multiples in frontier energy remain volatile. Investors should treat this range as directional rather than precise, pending additional market transactions or disclosed Series A terms from comparable companies.
